**Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship for this position.**

### **Job Description:**

Director, Executive Protection, Protective Operations and Logistics

The Role:

As the Director of Protective Operations and Logistics within the Executive Protection team, you will be responsible for executive protection program management and logistical planning, including staffing, scheduling*,* protective transportation operations, support request vetting and assessment, training administration, and oversight of the TSA Aircraft Security Officer (ASO) program. Reporting to the Head of Executive Protection, you will provide operational leadership, program oversight, and subject matter expertise on executive protection and protective operations matters. You willbe responsible for ensuring the effective execution of day-to-day protective operations while supporting the continued enhancement of the firm's executive protection capabilities. The position requires close collaboration with Global Security Operations, the Global Security Operations Center (GSOC), Travel Security, and key internal and external partners to implement and support Fidelity's executive protection strategy. Success in this role requires exceptional organizational, leadership, and relationship-management skills, as well as the ability to balance competing priorities while delivering consistent, discreet, and service-oriented experience for Fidelity's senior leadership.

The Expertise and Skills You Bring

* 7-10 years of experience protecting C-suite executives, board members, and/or government officials in complex, dynamic, and globally distributed operating environments within corporate, government, military, or law enforcement settings.
* Exceptional organizational and project management skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple workstreams
* Exceptional verbal, written, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with executives, business leaders, security professionals, and external stakeholders
* Extensive knowledge of executive protection operations, including protective advances, travel security, transportation security, venue assessment, route planning and protective operations logistics.
* Expertise in assessing, prioritizing, and coordinating executive support requests while balancing risk, resource requirements, and business priorities.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required and operate effectively in dynamic, rapidly changing, and high-pressure environments.
* Strong understanding of TSA Aircraft Security Officer (ASO) program requirements, administration, compliance, certifications, and operational integration; the ability to obtain and maintain ASO certification is highly preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to manage executive protection staffing models, personnel scheduling, resource allocation, and operational readiness across multiple locations and priorities.
* Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor, develop, and build high-performing teams while fostering a culture of professionalism, accountability, discretion, and service excellence.
* Experience coordinating and supporting executive travel, special events, corporate meetings, and other high-visibility engagements requiring detailed planning and collaboration.
* Experience managing executive transportation programs, including vehicle operations, driver standards, fleet utilization, and transportation security protocols.
* Experience developing and managing executive protection training programs, operational exercises, performance standards, readiness assessments, and professional development initiatives.
* Bachelor's degree is preferred; equivalent professional experience will be considered.
* Relevant professional certifications such as CTM, CPP, PSP, ASIS Executive Protection Professional (EPP), TSA ASO, or other intelligence, investigation, or executive protection credentials are a plus.
* undefined

The Purpose of Your Role

 

* Lead the planning, coordination, and execution of executive protection programs that ensure the safety, privacy, and operational effectiveness of Fidelity's executive leadership.
* Manage the day-to-day administration and logistical support of executive protection operations, including staffing, scheduling, executive travel, protective transportation, training, and resource allocation.
* Provide operational leadership and oversight for executive protection program management, ensuring consistent service delivery, operational readiness, and alignment with organizational priorities.
* Serve as a trusted partner to executive stakeholders by delivering responsive, discreet, and customer-focused protective services in support of business activities and executive requirements.
* Oversee the planning and coordination of executive travel, special events, site visits, and high-profile engagements, ensuring appropriate protective measures and logistical support are in place.
* Manage and enhance the TSA Aircraft Security Officer (ASO) program, executive transportation services, training initiatives, and other core executive protection capabilities.
* Serve as a trusted security advisor to senior executives, providing strategic guidance, risk-based recommendations, and executive-level briefings on protective operations, emerging threats, and security-related matters.

The Team

The Executive Protection team is part of the broader Protective Services team, which in turn is part of Fidelity’s Global Security team. The Executive Protection team is a highly valued team dedicated to the protection of the firm’s executive leadership and events.

Please be advised that Fidelity’s business is governed by the provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, ERISA, numerous state laws governing securities, investment and retirement-related financial activities and the rules and regulations of numerous self-regulatory organizations, including FINRA, among others. Those laws and regulations may restrict Fidelity from hiring and/or associating with individuals with certain Criminal Histories.

Fidelity’s Onsite Working Model 
Fidelity is transitioning to a full-time onsite working model through a phased rollout across regions and roles. Currently, some roles and locations require 100% onsite presence, while others require less. Onsite expectations are likely to evolve as the rollout continues. This transition does not apply to fully remote roles.

The base salary range for this position is $95,000-186,000 USD per year.

Placement in the range will vary based on job responsibilities and scope, geographic location, candidate’s relevant experience, and other factors.

Base salary is only part of the total compensation package. Depending on the position and eligibility requirements, the offer package may also include bonus or other variable compensation.

We offer a wide range of benefits to meet your evolving needs and help you live your best life at work and at home. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage and emotional well-being support, market-leading retirement, generous paid time off and parental leave, charitable giving employee match program, and educational assistance including student loan repayment, tuition reimbursement, and learning resources to develop your career. Note, the application window closes when the position is filled or unposted.

Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed. 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!    
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities. 
 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We're working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

 This role is part of Blue Origin's Launch Operations organization, where our focus is launching and recovering New Glenn safely, reliably, and at an ever-increasing cadence. Launch Operations owns everything required to turn a rocket into a flight-ready vehicle on the pad and to recover and refly it, from vehicle preparation and integration to pad operations and booster recovery.

 The 9x4 is the next step for New Glenn: a larger, more capable vehicle with a nine-engine booster, built, stacked, and launched vertically. The design decisions made about it now will determine, for the life of the program, how fast, how safely, and how reliably we can assemble, stack, and launch it. As Director of NG9x4 Vehicle Operations, you will be the single leader thinking about the 9x4 from the point of view of the people who will operate it, and the voice of Launch Operations in every decision meeting about the vehicle.
 Reporting to the Vice President of Launch Operations, you will start with a team of about a dozen engineers. Together you will evaluate the vehicle design and the concept of operations and shape both, help define and install the tooling and facilities in our new vertical integration facility, and write the first draft of the work orders for final assembly of the booster and for everything it takes to get the rocket to launch. Some of your scope will also reach the new launch pad being built for this vehicle. If you are successful, you will go on to build the organization that staffs the vertical integration facility and builds and stacks the first 9x4.

 This is a mission-critical leadership role for Blue Origin. We need a leader who drives relentlessly toward results, unencumbered by the old way of doing things, and constantly inventing new ways to solve problems and perform our mission. This leader must not be afraid to get hands-on with engineers and technicians, on the tooling, in the facility, and eventually on the vehicle itself, when the mission requires it, including in the middle of the night. At the same time, your long-term measure of success is building in, from the start, a vehicle and a set of processes that let the Launch Operations teams assemble, stack, and launch at a fast, repeatable, "boring" cadence. You'll make the impossible look routine through detailed, quantitative, hands-on command of the work your team executes down to the individual work order.
 


 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 Be the Voice of Operations on the 9x4 
 Represent Launch Operations in all design, configuration, and readiness decisions for the vehicle, bringing the perspective of the people who will assemble, stack, and launch it
 Evaluate the vehicle design and challenge requirements, driving design changes that make final assembly of the booster, stacking, and launch easier, faster, and safer
 Bring the lessons learned from today's horizontal integration operations into the design of vertical operations, and question which of them still apply
 Partner with vehicle design and engineering, facility, and pad teams so that operations needs are in the design before changes become expensive
 Stand Up Vertical Operations 
 Help shape the tooling, ground support equipment, and other installations in the new vertical integration facility, and help get them procured and installed
 Formalize the concept of operations in greater detail: how the nine-engine booster is finally assembled, how the second stage and payload are stacked vertically, and how the vehicle is prepared and launched
 Write the first draft of the work orders for final assembly of the booster and for all of the preparation needed to get the rocket to launch, and set the standard for high-quality, executable work orders (clear, sequenced, measurable, and completable by shift) so launch readiness is derived from objective data
 Take on operations scope for work at the new launch pad being built for this vehicle
 Lead Execution and Manage Risk 
 Manage technical and schedule risk as the vehicle, the facility, and the tooling come together; when schedule slips, personally own and drive the recovery plan rather than simply reporting the slip
 Perpetuate a high-standard safety culture across all vehicle work, given the significant personnel, process, and material hazards involved
 Be willing to get on the ground with engineers and technicians to solve problems directly, at any hour, when the mission requires it
 Drive Cross-Functional Integration 
 Serve as the primary point of contact between the operations teams and New Glenn vehicle design/engineering, facility, tooling, and pad leadership
 Partner with the business operations function (scheduling and operations analytics) to maintain an objective, data-driven view of remaining work and schedule risk
 Build the organization's own engineering ownership and judgment over time, reducing reliance on borrowed engineering support from other Blue Origin programs
 Build and Lead a High-Performing Organization 
 Lead an initial team of about a dozen engineers, and grow it into the organization that staffs the vertical integration facility and builds and stacks the first 9x4
 Build, mentor, and develop a bench of leaders and engineers in a fast-growing organization
 Take difficult, immature processes and mature them into fast, repeatable operations that don't require nightly heroics to execute
 Foster a culture where every technician and engineer is genuinely excited about Blue Origin's mission and understands the "why" behind the work
 Champion the use of AI to reduce engineering workload (including work-order authoring) and to accelerate the ramp of less experienced engineers
 Deliver Results 
 Use your own data and numerical analysis to understand team performance, drive decisions, and communicate progress
 Set quantitative targets for the labor hours and calendar time to assemble, stack, and launch the 9x4, and shape the vehicle and the processes to meet them, so the vehicle supports a much higher launch cadence
 Present vehicle design, readiness, and risk to Blue Origin's most senior executive leadership, including with little to no coaching
 
 WHAT YOU BRING

 Minimum Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or Industrial Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience building and leading complex vehicle or aircraft programs
 7+ years of progressive leadership experience building, integrating, or maintaining complex vehicles, aircraft, or other high-reliability systems: aerospace, defense, marine, oil & gas, or similar heavy/complex-machine environments
 Experience representing operations, manufacturing, or production in design decisions, with a demonstrated track record of challenging engineering requirements and driving design changes to improve manufacturability or maintainability
 Leadership experience with budget and resource management responsibility for technical/operational organizations
 Experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams, with the ability to grow a team and lead through subordinate managers
 A specific, demonstrated track record of driving measurable rate or throughput improvements in a complex manufacturing, assembly, or operations environment
 A demonstrated track record of building and perpetuating a high-standard safety culture in environments with significant personnel, process, or material hazards
 Demonstrated ability to make high-stakes technical and operational decisions under schedule pressure
 Strong executive presence with excellent written and verbal communication skills; demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all levels, including senior executive leadership
 Strategic thinker with a bias for action and a track record of hands-on operational execution
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Direct experience in final assembly, integration, or maintenance of military or civilian aircraft, weapons systems, or launch vehicles
 Experience with vertical assembly or stacking of large vehicles or structures, such as launch vehicles, or comparable heavy lifting and integration
 Experience standing up a new factory, production line, or facility, including shaping the tooling and the concept of operations
 Experience writing the first work instructions or work orders for a new vehicle or product
 A track record of taking a new vehicle, aircraft, or complex product from first-unit production to rate production
 Hands-on experience as an aircraft mechanic (or similar trade) and/or as a manufacturing engineer
 Working knowledge of aerospace standards and workmanship requirements
 Experience building or scaling an engineering/technical organization from a nascent, dependent state to self-sufficiency
 Master's degree in a related engineering field, or an MBA
 Culture Statement 
 Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Export Control Regulations 
 Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 Background Check 
 Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
 Required for Certain Job Profiles:  Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
 Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
 Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical
 
 Benefits 
 Benefits include:  Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
 Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
 Paid Time Off:  Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
 Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
 Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here .

 Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation 
 Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at  EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
The Plant Manager is responsible for coordinating, directing, leading, guiding, and managing areas of the plant consistent with company policies and procedures as well as with federal, state and local law. Will be accountable for the management and safety of employees, high quality products being produced, budgeting and the profitability of the facility. The Plant Manager develops processes that will maximize stewardship, safety, quality, culture, customer relations, and productivity. This role has direct supervisory responsibility for all operations management and hourly team members with an expanded dotted line responsibility for a variety of support groups when department heads are not present (i.e., Sanitation, Shipping, Maintenance & Engineering). Will work closely with Human Resources and production teams in hire and train staff.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**: This list is not intended to be all-inclusive and other duties may be assigned.

* Initiate and maintain a safe workplace in accordance with regulatory and plant policies by maintaining effective safety and ergonomic programs and proactively correcting deficiencies to meet company goals of an injury free workplace.
* Responsible for communicating necessary feedback updates, up through STF leadership that pertain to the shift's activities.
* Be an active member, leading and facilitating our Safety Committee.
* Implement and attain goals to reduce injuries and cost per claim of injuries.
* Responsible for team members for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of all shift operations; ensure all operating procedures are followed and correct and/or update when needed.
* Ensure employee safety training, assist in the identification of and correction of safety hazards and ergonomic issues.
* Ensure all staff and employees know and understand CCP's, HACCP and SSOP documents/plans.
* Maintain product failures and foreign material issues are kept at a minimum; continue efforts for improvement.
* Responsible for overseeing all plant activity within all departments of the shift including supporting areas.
* Serve as a contact person for vendors and suppliers.
* Initiate and modify as necessary methods of ensuring production goals are met, including product quality per food safety requirements and specifications, efficiency, hours, cost and safety to remain efficient and competitive.
* Develop and manage a system that tracks labor, product and packaging costs that result in a reduction to the budget.
* Carries out managerial/supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the companies policies and applicable laws.
* Responsible for plant labor, raw material utilization, yields, supplies and waste reduction to ensure they are being managed in the most efficient manner.
* Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, training employees, planning, directing and assigning work; appraising performance; rewarding and counseling employees when necessary to maintain a high standard of employee relations.
* Facilitate training and development sessions that develops the skills and education of company leaders.
* Develop and manage a strong productive working relationship with the UFCW, Local 2. Ensuring compliance with our collective bargaining agreement.

**QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS**: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the work environment, knowledge, skill, and/or ability required or preferred. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**: Bachelor's degree in a related field (agriculture, animal science or business) plus ten years of plant experience or the combination of education and experience that enables performance in all aspects of the position, including supervisory experience. Well-developed management skills utilizing sound management principles in leading a team of employees.

**COMMUNICATION SKILLS**: Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to write reports and business correspondence. Ability to effectively manage time and meet all specified deadlines.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS**: Ability to read and interpret documents in the English language such as safety files, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Must be able to effectively communicate with USDA, production and management personnel.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS**: Ability to apply mathematical applications to practical situations.

**REASONING ABILITY**: Ability to solve practical problems. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram or schedule form.

**OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES**: Ability to use computers and all standard programs used by the industry and the ability to learn and effectively use any and all other computer programs that are or will be made available.

**BACKUP PERSONNEL**: In the absence of the Plant Manager, the Plant Superintendent will assume responsibilities for overseeing food safety and quality assurance programs.

**MISSION, VISION, & VALUES:** Must believe and lead STF's **MISSION** of producing quality pork products, igniting the passion and growth of our team members, helping our community thrive, and making our business prosperous. Remembering that together we will achieve more by working safely and cultivating an inclusive and empowering environment. Must believe and fully engage in STF's **VISION** of being a place where we all belong, working as one, to build our future. Must live STF's **VALUES** in all decisions, behaviors, and interactions, which include-

SAFETY- Be committed to the safety and welfare of all employees through prevention, education, and awareness, with the ultimate goal of eliminating workplace accidents.

QUALITY- Our customers and families depend on us to provide a safe, quality product, by maintaining the highest food safety standards and desired customer specifications. Must take pride in the products we produce and serve.

DIVERSITY- We embrace diversity of identity, experience, and thought, and actively strive for inclusive behaviors across our company and our work. By promoting these values, we aim to create a positive work experience that encourage a sense of belonging.

COMMUNITY- Be a positive representative of STF in our community while supporting the organizations who work for the betterment of Siouxland.

SUSTAINABILITY- Be a steward of the earth by managing our environmental footprint.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**: While performing the duties of this job, the employee will be required to move about the facility. The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; use hands to finger; handle; or feel/hold objects; reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; speak; hear taste and smell. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Individual must be able to effectively work in a normal production environment where temperatures and noise levels may vary.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**Definition:**

The Director of Operations is responsible for planning, directing, and coordinating the overall field operations of a business unit throughout a designated geographical area. Duties and responsibilities include formulating processes and best practices, managing daily operations and clinical compliance, and effectively and efficiently planning and executing the use of equipment, materials, and personnel to best meet the needs of customers, facilities, and the community in which it serves.

**Specific Duties:**

* Demonstrates complete knowledge, understanding and compliance of company policies and procedures.
* Works with the Business Leaders on developing strategic plan.
* Works with Business Leaders on developing and meeting annual budget.
* Responsible for overall profit and loss management of operations.
* Responsible for managing local vendor relations and accounts payable management.
* Responsible for monitoring staffing levels in all operations in order to maintain operational efficiency.
* Ensures that all field staff maintain a high level of customer service when dealing with patients, patient families, co-responders, other healthcare providers and the general public.
* Ensures that all field staff in all operations maintain appropriate certification and licensure for their position.
* Ensures security and privacy of all company and patient information at all times in accordance HIPPA and all other local, state and federal regulations.
* Ensures that all operations are in full compliance with all local, state and federal regulations regarding the ordering, storage, use and record keeping of controlled substances.
* Ensures that all operations are in full compliance with all company policies regarding clinical protocols and field documentation.
* Ensures that all operations are in full compliance with all local, state and federal contracts, regulations and ordinances.
* Displays a positive mental attitude toward the position held, the company, and its employees, clients, partners or affiliates.
* Clearly, effectively, and professionally express him/herself verbally and in writing,
* Responds to all incidents involving serious personal injury, excessive damage to company equipment or excessive damage to private property involving company personnel or equipment.
* Monitor the use of services, vehicles, equipment, facilities, and staff to ensure effective use of resources and assess the need for additional staff, equipment, and services.
* Review and analyze facility activities and data to aid planning and risk management to improve service utilization and quality.
* Direct, supervise and evaluate work activities of all personnel assigned to the Operations Division.
* Facilitate communication between EMS staff, support staff, and members of management as appropriate.
* Establish and implement operations division policies, goals, objectives, and procedures.
* Review financial statements, sales and activity reports, and other performance data to measure productivity and goal achievement and to determine areas needing cost reduction and program improvement.
* Responsible for annual re-certification of all ambulances.
* Maintains and ensures compliance of Standard Operating Procedures for all company operations.
* Ensures completion of annual skills evaluation for all personnel as needed.
* Assists other division directors as needed.
* Develop and maintain computerized record management systems to store, process data, and produce reports, such as personnel activities and information.
* Coordinate activities as appropriate with other division leaders concerned with reference to pricing, sales, training, human resources or distribution of services.
* Determine staffing requirements, and assist other division directors with interviewing, hiring and training new employees as needed.
* Maintain awareness of advances in EMS diagnostic and treatment equipment, data processing technology, government regulations, health insurance changes, and financing options.
* Performs other duties as directed by management.

#IND1

**Minimum Requirements:**

* All Paramedic requirements (Current Paramedic Certification)
 + Must possess a high degree of personal integrity and responsibility.
 + Currently licensed, certified or registered by the appropriate state agencies.
 + Currently certified in CPR by the AHA or other appropriate organization.
 + Currently certified in ACLS, PALS and/or other specialty certifications as required.
 + Currently licensed with the appropriate level of state motor vehicle operator’s license.
 + Currently has a clean driving record in accordance with company standards.
 + Must have and demonstrate the ability to work effectively with minimal supervision, using good judgment.
 + Must have and demonstrate the ability to work efficiently and interact in a constructive and professional manner with other employees, public safety personnel and medical staff.
 + Must have and demonstrate the ability to interact effectively and professionally with patients, customers, clients, family members, bystanders, and the general public in such a manner as to reflect positively on the company.
 + Must demonstrate a level of skill and ability consistent with the provision of high-quality patient care.
 + Must have and demonstrate the ability to perform effectively as team leader and team member in patient care situations.
 + Must have and demonstrate the ability to perform effectively in carrying out public relations and community education functions with members of the medical community and general public in promoting the company.
* All Paramedic Field Supervisor requirements
* Must have and demonstrate the ability function as a leader evaluating, coaching, training and directing field staff.
* Must have and demonstrate solid business management and administrative skills

**Physical Requirements:**

* The ability to reach, push and pull.
* The ability to sit or stand for long periods of time.
* The ability to complete all job duties during any and all hours of the day and night.
* The ability to use mouse or keyboard to input data into computer over long periods of time.
* The ability to view graphic and text data on multiple computer screens for long periods of times.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril Intelligence Systems (AIS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized engineering and products for Intelligence Community (IC) customers. We work within the IC to understand their requirements, shape their concepts of operation, and deliver exquisite capability across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 We are looking for a Head of Operations to join our rapidly growing Intelligence Systems team. In this role you will be responsible for all business operations for the business line you support. Your work will vary from quick-turn operational fire-fighting, to building and redesigning processes, to leading high-impact strategic projects. This role requires you to be a trusted partner to each part of the business, and to work with and support the Division leadership teams to achieve our strategic objectives.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

 
 Partner to the GM — Serve as the right hand to the General Manager of Intelligence Systems, responsible for all internal operations of the business line.

 Act as COO of the business line — Drive day-to-day business operations for Intelligence Systems. This includes business planning & organization design, financial tracking, talent planning & people operations, staffing and hiring, corporate governance, go-to-market, real estate & facility planning, security & infrastructure compliance, proposal & legal support, and sharing the division's narrative — working with cross-functional partners across each of these domains.

 Lead the BizOps team — Lead the Business Operations team within Intelligence Systems, composed of a Business Execution/Services team and Business Analytics, with the potential to include Production Operations/Analytics.

 Own the bottom line — Own the business line P&L and burn rate. Partner with Finance and FP&A to track financial health against division goals, take action to keep operating expenses within budget, and recommend strategies to drive toward margin targets.

 Define growth strategy — Define the growth strategy for Intelligence Systems in partnership with the Intelligence Systems Leadership Team, and lead strategic initiatives in line with business line priorities.

 Enable the engineering mission — Support the growth, execution, and engineering of the business line with operational support.

 Scale the organization — Problem solve to enable the business line to operate as efficiently as possible and scale accordingly.

 Represent the business externally — Build senior leader engagement and external interface strategy (e.g., conferences, press releases, partnerships).

 Build partnerships — Build, negotiate, and execute partnerships across industry.

 Support M&A activity — Identify targets and engage in diligence.

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 10-15+ years of professional experience in operations.

 Strong communication skills; trusted by executives and colleagues alike — Demonstrated ability to translate and articulate thoughts clearly and simply across a wide range of roles (software engineers, finance partners, recruiters, cross-functional leadership, and executives). Communications excellence across a wide dynamic range, both written and verbal. Experience interfacing with company leadership and executives is a must, with a demonstrated ability to cultivate trust, facilitate meetings for, and engage with executives.

 Technically minded — Solid technical aptitude and proven ability to understand technical designs, and the ability to work closely and effectively with engineering teams.

 Bridges operational and analytical teams — Strong emotional intelligence and ability to solve operational problems in a way that is both data-driven and people-centric.

 High ownership and capacity — Horsepower to effectively manage multiple (6+) large projects and priorities in parallel, at a rapid pace, and report out on progress regularly.

 Finance literate — Comfortable owning a bottom line, reading and acting on P&L, budget, and margin data in partnership with FP&A.

 Ability to work onsite five days a week at either our Reston, VA office or our HQ in Costa Mesa, CA.

 Minimum 25% travel expected.

 Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 MBA or similar degree.

 Experience working with engineers and bringing hardware/software products to market strongly preferred.

 Experience in the intelligence community or national security mission space

 Experience leading a business operations, business analytics, or similar function

 Experience working effectively in a matrix organization structure.

 Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related field.

 US Salary Range
 $183,000 — $243,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: 

 

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

 

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


 

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ . 

 

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available 
 
CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No 
 
CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret 
 
TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description 
 
At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. 
 
 
 The Director, Manufacturing Engineering provides functional and strategic leadership for the manufacturing engineering organization, accountable for process capability, producibility, and product quality across production programs. This role leads a team of managers and engineers responsible for developing, deploying, and continuously improving manufacturing, test, and related industrial engineering processes to meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people objectives in Baltimore, MD .

 Key Responsibilities
 Functional & People Leadership Lead and develop a high‑performing manufacturing engineering organization, including managers, engineers, and supporting staff.
 Define and maintain functional standards, methods, tools, and best practices for manufacturing engineering across the site or business.
 Recruit, develop, and retain talent; drive succession planning, leadership development, and engagement/inclusion activities.
 Provide regular coaching, performance feedback, and career development for managers and engineers.
 
 
 Manufacturing Engineering Ownership Own manufacturing engineering processes from new product introduction through sustainment, ensuring robust process controls, standard work, and documented work instructions.
 Direct the creation and maintenance of MBOMs, routings, work instructions, tooling, and strategies that enable safe, efficient, and high‑quality production.
 Drive producibility into designs by partnering with Design Engineering early in the lifecycle; ensure effective transition to production and rate readiness.
 Establish and manage key performance indicators (yields, scrap, rework, cycle time, labor efficiency) and drive continuous improvement using data‑driven methods.
 
 
 Operations, Quality, and Continuous Improvement Partner closely with Operations, Quality & Mission Excellence, and Supply Chain to ensure stable processes and timely resolution of production issues.
 Oversee manufacturing engineering participation in MRB and nonconformance disposition; ensure effective root‑cause analysis and corrective/preventive actions.
 Champion initiatives to improve safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
 Lead manufacturing engineering support to factory readiness, capacity planning, and rate ramp‑ups.
 
 
 Program, Financial, and Strategic Management Align functional objectives, resources, and priorities with program and business needs; balance near‑term execution with long‑term capability development.
 Partner with Program Management and Business Management to support bids, proposals, and program execution, including manufacturing scope, risk, and cost/schedule inputs.
 Own manufacturing engineering budgets (labor, capital, and expense) and apply sound financial management.
 Develop and execute technology roadmaps and capital investment plans for manufacturing processes, equipment, and facilities.
 
 
 Compliance, Governance, and Stakeholder Management Ensure manufacturing engineering processes comply with regulatory requirements, customer standards, and internal procedures.
 Represent manufacturing engineering in internal and external reviews, audits, and customer engagements.
 Build strong relationships with sector/site leadership, program teams, and functional peers to drive alignment and resolve cross‑functional constraints.
 
 
 Basic Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related discipline with 10 or more years of relevant experience; OR a Master’s degree in Engineering or a related discipline with 8 or more years of relevant experience.
 3 or more years of functional management experience leading organizations of at least 100 employees.
 Progressive leadership experience in manufacturing/production, operations, program management, testing, or a related area, including direct leadership of engineers and/or first‑line managers.
 Demonstrated experience in manufacturing or production engineering supporting complex hardware (e.g., aerospace, defense, electronics, or similar).
 Proven track record of improving manufacturing and test processes, yields, cycle times, and product quality using data and metrics.
 Working knowledge of manufacturing process controls, quality systems, and relevant industry/regulatory standards.
 Demonstrated financial acumen including budgets, rates, and cost management
 Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly present technical and operational content to leadership and customers.
 U.S. citizenship and an ability to obtain U.S. Government Secret security clearance or greater; OR DoE equivalent or greater
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Advanced degree in Engineering, Engineering Management, Business Administration, or related field.
 Experience in a Director or senior manager role leading a manufacturing engineering or test engineering organization in an aerospace/defense or similarly regulated environment.
 Experience working across multiple disciplines (design, manufacturing, and test engineering) with a strong focus on product development, producibility, and transition to production.
 Hands‑on experience with continuous improvement frameworks
 Experience managing capital equipment roadmaps and facilities upgrades to support long‑term manufacturing capacity and capability.
 Proven ability to build and develop high‑performing teams, including succession planning, leadership development, and engagement initiatives.
 Experience supporting proposals and customer reviews, including articulation of manufacturing engineering approaches, risks, and mitigations.
 Experience working in a matrixed organization, balancing program demands with functional standards and development needs.
 
 
 
Primary Level Salary Range: $194,600.00 - $292,000.00 
 
The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions. 
 
Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business. 
 
The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. 
 
Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.

The Solutions Architect is expected to be the trusted advisor and go-to resource for Manufacturing and Quality business partners on any process change involving Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Planning or the MES, QMS, and PLM bolt-on applications — translating business need into a scalable, well-architected solution, and then configuring and implementing that solution directly for medium-complexity projects. For large, complex initiatives, this person leads solution design and partners with Shield AI’s implementation partner to deliver, while remaining the accountable architect and voice of the business throughout.
Beyond core ERP, this role holds full ownership of Shield AI’s manufacturing-adjacent bolt-on application landscape — including MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter) — and is responsible for how those systems integrate with Oracle Fusion ERP to form a coherent plan-to-build-to-quality operating model. This role partners closely with the other Solutions Architects for Supply Chain and Finance on shared MRP/planning signals, supplier quality matters tied to Procure-to-Pay and end-to-end integration with Finance/Accounting.

What you'll do: 
Solution Architecture & Business Partnership
Designs and delivers technical solutions, creates detailed solution designs, specific integration points, and selects appropriate tools and frameworks. Collaboration with developers and engineers to implement solutions, conducts technical reviews and resolves design challenges.
Documents architectures, provides technical guidance during development, and ensures solutions adhere to performance, security, and interoperability requirements. Prototypes new approaches and evaluates emerging technologies for project suitability.
Serve as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor for business partners across Manufacturing, Production Planning, Quality, and Engineering on process design and system capability questions.
Act as the lead advocate for Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders in all ERP, MES, QMS, and PLM-related discussions, ensuring their operational needs, constraints, and priorities are represented in solution design.
Become the go-to resource for any proposed Manufacturing or Quality process change, evaluating impact, feasibility, and fit within the Oracle Fusion ERP data model and integration landscape before implementation.
Translate business requirements into scalable solution designs that balance standard Oracle Fusion functionality against configuration, extension, or integration needs.
Maintain a working command of adjacent end-to-end flows (Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay) to ensure Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS designs do not create downstream conflicts or gaps.
Hands-On Configuration & Delivery
Directly configure Oracle Fusion Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning/MRP, Work Definitions, Quality Inspections, and related modules for medium-sized projects, enhancements, and break/fix work.
Build, test, and deploy configuration changes, including setup of Fusion functional areas, security, workflows, approval rules, and data structures related to manufacturing and planning processes.
Author functional design documents, configuration workbooks, test scripts, and process/procedure documentation to support changes made in the environment.
For large or highly complex initiatives, define solution architecture and requirements, then partner closely with the implementation partner to execute — remaining accountable for solution quality, business fit, and knowledge transfer.
Participate in and help lead workshops, fit-gap sessions, and design reviews with Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders and implementation partner teams.
MRP, MES & QMS Ownership
Own MRP and Supply Chain Planning configuration — planning parameters, supply/demand netting, exception messages, and planner workbench — ensuring plans translate cleanly into executable work orders.
Own the functional roadmap, configuration governance, and business alignment for:
– MES (Manufacturing Execution System) — work order execution, shop-floor data collection, routing/operation tracking
– QMS (Quality Management System) — inspections, non-conformance, corrective/preventive action (CAPA), supplier quality
– PLM – Teamcenter — engineering BOM, item master, and change management integration with Oracle Fusion
Ensure MES, QMS, and PLM remain architecturally aligned with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP, avoiding duplicate data ownership, conflicting BOM/routing data, or process gaps across systems.
Define and maintain the target integration model between MES, QMS, PLM, and Oracle Fusion ERP, including engineering-to-manufacturing BOM transfer and quality event-to-ERP disposition flows.
Partner with the Solutions Architect – Supply Chain on supplier-quality data flowing from Procure-to-Pay into QMS-driven supplier corrective action processes.
Integrations
Design and help implement integrations between Oracle Fusion ERP and MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter), including BOM/routing sync, work order status, and quality disposition data.
Define integration requirements, data mappings, and error-handling/reconciliation approaches in partnership with technical/integration teams.
Evaluate integration patterns (API, middleware, file-based) and recommend approaches appropriate to data volume, latency, and criticality, particularly for shop-floor/real-time data.
Support testing, cutover, and hypercare activities for integration-related changes.
Governance & Continuous Improvement
Maintain configuration standards, documentation, and change control discipline for the Manufacturing, MRP, MES, QMS, and PLM functional areas.
Identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved data quality across planning, production, and quality cycles.
Stay current on Oracle Fusion quarterly releases relevant to Manufacturing and Planning, and assess/recommend adoption of new features.
Mentor junior functional/technical resources and contribute to a growing internal ERP center of excellence.
Required Qualifications:
12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise ERP systems, with significant depth in MRP/Supply Chain Planning, MES, and QMS functions.
Hands-on experience configuring Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP (Manufacturing and Planning pillars); comfortable working directly in the application, not solely at a requirements level.
Experience across multiple full-lifecycle ERP implementations (Oracle Fusion required; prior experience with Oracle EBS, SAP, or other major ERP platforms is a plus).
Direct, hands-on experience with at least one MES platform and one QMS platform, including their integration into an ERP environment.
Working knowledge of Order-to-Cash and Procure-to-Pay processes and how they interact with Manufacturing, MRP, and quality operations.
Demonstrated experience acting as a functional/solution architect — able to design solutions independently, not just execute configuration tasks handed down by others.
Experience partnering with or managing systems integrators/implementation partners on complex delivery efforts.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills; comfortable being the primary escalation point for Manufacturing and Quality process questions.
Working understanding of integration concepts and experience partnering on ERP-to-MES/QMS/PLM system integrations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing functional design documents, process documentation, and executive-level updates.
Preferred Qualifications:
Prior consulting background (Big 4, Oracle partner, or boutique Oracle Fusion implementation firm) strongly preferred.
Direct experience owning or integrating PLM (Teamcenter) with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Engineering data.
Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated/complex discrete manufacturing environments.
Familiarity with Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) or similar middleware/integration platforms.
Oracle Fusion certifications in Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning, or Quality.
Experience operating in environments with export control, ITAR/CUI, or other regulated data-handling requirements.
AI & Agentic Automation Capabilities:
Shield AI is investing in Agentic AI to accelerate and automate manufacturing and quality operations. This role is expected to actively identify, design, and help implement AI-driven automation across Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS — not simply consume AI tools built by others.
Identify high-value candidates for Agentic AI automation within Manufacturing and Quality — e.g., planner workbench exception triage, shop-floor anomaly detection, quality non-conformance routing/CAPA drafting, and work order scheduling recommendations.
Design and configure AI agent workflows using Oracle’s embedded AI/ML and agentic capabilities (e.g., Oracle Fusion AI agents, OCI Generative AI, Redwood/AI-driven planning recommendations) as they become available across Fusion Manufacturing and Planning.
Partner with IT/data teams to define prompts, guardrails, data inputs, and approval/exception paths for AI agents acting on manufacturing and quality transactions, ensuring appropriate human-in-the-loop controls.
Evaluate and pilot third-party or custom Agentic AI tools (e.g., for predictive maintenance, quality defect pattern detection, MES data synthesis, or supply/demand sensing) and assess fit against the target architecture.
Use AI-assisted tools for day-to-day solution work — requirements analysis, test script generation, configuration documentation, and data mapping — to increase delivery speed and quality.
Bring or build fluency in prompt engineering and AI workflow design; prior hands-on experience with generative AI or agentic AI platforms (Oracle AI Agent Studio, OCI Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, UiPath/Automation Anywhere agentic features, or similar) is a strong plus.
Champion responsible AI adoption — data quality, auditability, and change management — when introducing agentic workflows into regulated, ITAR/CUI-sensitive environments.

*Are you a passionate leader energized by driving continuous improvement?* ***Winnebago Motorhome is seeking a Plant Manager to join our team based in Forest City, IA.*** *The Plant Manager leads overall operations of a soft goods manufacturing facility (cut-and-sew, upholstery, foam, and textile assembly). This expert-level role owns safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people (SQDCP) performance, deploying lean manufacturing systems (5S, Standard Work, Visual Management, Kaizen) and ensuring compliance with relevant standards (RVIA, OSHA, NFPA 1192, ANSI methods as applicable). Responsibilities include strategic planning, capacity and labor management, production scheduling, quality systems oversight, supplier and materials coordination, cross-department alignment, and talent development to achieve world-class operational results.*

**Day to Day of the Role:**

* Own plant SQDCP performance; establish and drive KPIs and tiered daily management (Safety, OEE, FPY, on-time delivery, productivity, scrap, rework, etc).
* Lead daily Tier 1-3 process, Gemba walks, huddles, and visual management; drive corrective actions and sustainment.
* Implement and sustain lean systems: 5S, Standard Work, Kanban/pull systems, value stream mapping, line balancing, takt-time alignment, TPM. (Lean Six Sigma Blackbelt Preferred but not required)
* Ensure compliance with industry and regulatory requirements: Industry and lean best practices, RVIA, OSHA, EHS, NFPA 1192, and ANSI methods as applicable.
* Oversee master scheduling, capacity planning, labor planning, and materials flow to meet demand with optimal lead time and cost.
* Champion quality: PFMEA/Control Plans, incoming/in-process/final inspection, root cause analysis (8D, DMAIC), containment, and standardization.
* Optimize cutting, kitting, sewing, upholstery, and final assembly workflows; reduce WIP, increase throughput, and minimize waste.
* Manage budget, P&L elements, cost reduction, and productivity projects; implement make/buy and outsourcing strategies as needed.
* Build and mentor high-performing supervisors and hourly teams; certify skills; conduct performance reviews; drive cross-training and succession planning.
* Partner with Engineering on DFM/DFA; manage ECNs, prototypes, and ramp-to-rate.
* Own, develop, and mentor best practices for inventory and processes.
* Collaborate with Supply Chain on supplier performance, material availability, and packaging standards.
* Enforce safety culture: risk assessments (JSA), ergonomics, PPE, incident investigations, and compliance training.
* Lead continuous improvement events (Kaizen) and audits; maintain document control and training records.
* Coordinate with Customer Service/Program Management for priorities, promise dates, and escalations; communicate status and recovery plans.

**Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field preferred.
* Associate’s degree with significant relevant experience will also be considered.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations.
* 7–10+ years of people management experience, including leading teams through change.
* Moderate to in-depth knowledge of Tools, Machines, or Equipment Required (Mechanical and digital measuring and inspection tools, tape, calipers, tension gauges, fabric weight/yardage tools, color/finish checks).
* ERP (D365) or similar modern Operations and Finance manufacturing software
* Basic office systems for analytics, drawings/specs, and work instructions.
* Practical understanding and ability to perform with Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, Word, NX & Team Center (or similar engineering software)

 Raytheon has an opening for a Sr. Production Control Lead supporting our Undersea Factory in our Portsmouth, RI facility. The successful candidate has experience with Material Requirements Planning (MRP) systems in a manufacturing environment and utilizes data-driven decision making to enable effective material and workforce forecasting. This role requires daily interaction with cross functional teams, programs, and business units to maintain and meet organizational goals and objectives. These groups include planning, production control, operations, quality, and manufacturing/test/design engineering.
  
  
 What You Will Do 
 Managing a highly visible area with 6 production control professionals reporting into this position.
 Set strategic vision, direction and plan to execute on short to medium term program and functional strategies and initiatives.
 Material Availability Analysis, Tracking, and Reporting.
 Manage Kit Readiness including working with cross-functional team in BOM, Material Master, Process Engineering, Operations, and Document Control.
 Releasing production schedules in multiple tools through the MRP system and confirming in shop floor system.
 Coordinates kitting process with multiple stores and consolidation areas.
 Provide production floor support including replacement part management, shop floor material staging, Work in Progress (WIP) movement through shared resource areas, completion of units in shop floor and MRP system, delivery to next step (inventory or shipment), and meeting MRP schedule.
 Control the physical disposition of nonconforming or specially handled material including Return to Vendor, purged material, WIP STOP per contractual restrictions, and configuration of components/sub-assemblies as required.
 Maintain integrity of the shop floor, MRP, and inventory systems through key performance metrics.
 Process piece part movement to support internal build requirements through subcontractors, internal shared resources, and other Raytheon Technologies facilities.
 This position is an onsite role in our Portsmouth, RI facility.
   
   
 Qualifications You Must Have 
 Typically requires A University Degree or equivalent experience and minimum 10 years prior relevant experience, or An Advanced Degree in a related field and minimum 7 years experience.
 Experience in Production Control, Supply Chain, Planning, Logistics, Scheduling, Operations, Manufacturing, or other production driven environments within manufacturing.  
 Experience with MRP/ERP systems.
 Experience leading daily team operations and/or comparable leadership experience.
  
  
 Qualifications We Prefer 
 Experience leading in a Department of Defense (DoD) environment.
 Experience in Special Program Access and other business systems, including shop floor data systems.
 Experience in Six Sigma, CORE, Lean Manufacturing processes, diagnostics, and continuous improvement.
 Experience driving financial performance, cost reduction, staffing, and budgeting.

* **Plant-Floor Engagement:** Build a strong IT presence in the plants through regular plant visits, operational reviews, and frontline engagement. Ensure IT teams understand production processes.

* **Operational Reliability:** Establish accountability for the availability and resilience of plant IT. Partner across IT to eliminate recurring issues, address root causes, and minimize disruption.

* **Technology Delivery & Site Readiness:** Provide Plant IT leadership for initiatives from planning and readiness through deployment, stabilization, adoption, and transition to support.

* **Portfolio & Priority Management:** Partner with Manufacturing and IT leaders to identify, prioritize, and govern plant technology demand. Balance safety, business continuity, and operational risk, regulatory requirements, business value, capacity, dependencies, and strategic alignment.

* **Standardization & Simplification:** Establish common Plant IT processes, standards, documentation, escalation practices, support models, and deployment.

* **Cross-Functional Coordination:** Act as an integration point among Plant Operations, Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Manufacturing Technology, and Supply Chain.

* **Lifecycle, Governance & Risk:** Maintain visibility to plant technology assets, application dependencies, lifecycle risks, obsolescence, supportability, and cybersecurity exposure. Establish governance and escalation for risks that could affect production or business continuity.

* **Continuous Improvement & Innovation:** Identify opportunities to improve plant performance through better use of existing technology, process simplification, digital capabilities, and data.

* **Service Management:** Establish consistent expectations for incident, problem, change. Use service metrics, production-impact analysis, and recurring issue trends to improve Plant IT performance.

* **Executive Communication:** Provide concise, outcome-oriented visibility to Manufacturing and IT leadership regarding technology performance, major incidents, investment priorities, and value.

* **People & Culture:** Build a high-performing, collaborative Plant IT organization through clear expectations, coaching, career development, succession planning, accountability.
 

 

**WHAT WE’RE SEEKING:**

*To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential functions.*

* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor's Degree from an accredited four-year college or university and 10+ years of relevant experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience, required.
* **Leadership Experience:** 5+ years of experience in team management/development required.
* **Manufacturing Expertise:** Hands-on experience with manufacturing systems is required, including MES, SCADA, automation, quality control, labeling, or compliance systems.
* **Technical Knowledge:** Proven experience leading teams that support and troubleshoot industrial PCs, labelers, scales, and RF scanning equipment.
* **Problem-Solving & Analysis:** Strong critical thinking, decision-making, and analytical problem-solving skills; self-directed and proactive in identifying solutions.
* **Collaboration & Communication:** Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with a proven ability to work across all levels of the organization and cross-functional teams.
* **Work Environment & Travel:** Must be able to travel up to 30%, depending on project and plant support needs.
* **Organizational Skills:** Strong organizational abilities with a track record of managing complex initiatives effectively.
* **Work Style & Values:** Respectful, approachable, and team-oriented, with a focus on fostering a positive work environment and strong working relationships.
